items.title: Objects of a Grothendieck abelian category are small for large cofinality
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file injectives.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that an object of a Grothendieck abelian category with at most kappa subobjects is alpha-small with respect to injections for every ordinal alpha of cofinality bigger than kappa (statement lines 1633-1639). The proof is a complete argument mirroring the module case: it suffices to show a displayed comparison map is surjective (proof lines 1641-1644); the source of a map into the colimit is written as the union of the preimages of the stages, which reduces the statement to those preimages (proof lines 1644-1655); and the set of stages whose preimages cover a fixed preimage is bounded in cardinality by the number of subobjects, so the cofinality hypothesis gives an upper bound stage and the factorisation follows (proof lines 1656-1667). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping of the preimages. The claim is H2.
